thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU queue > 95th percentile for customer 'medica' on private cluster cluster-17 (dublin). autoscaler failing to add nodes; queue length increasing. Paging oncall.
jamal: oncall here — taking it.
jamal: quick triage: all inference queues for medica are piling up for the last ~4m. throughput drops, requests are getting 429/503 intermittently.
jamal: metrics snapshot:
```
- gpu_queue_length: 142 -> 315 over 4m
- infra.autoscaler.desired: 20
- infra.autoscaler.current: 12
- infra.autoscaler.pending_nodes: 8
- autoscaler.rate_limit: 1 node/sec
- nodeprovision.errors: PXE_TIMEOUT x78, IMAGE_PULL_DELAY x24
```
sara: is this isolated to medica or broader?
jamal: looks isolated to cluster-17 and nodepool "m-rtx-pool" (onprem). other customers in same region are fine.
carmen: logs from autoscaler? can you paste the last 50 lines?
jamal: pasted relevant tail below — main recurring error is "node boot timed out" and "waiting for BMC inventory"
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:13Z] autoscaler: provisioning node node-rtx-45 state=BOOTING
[2026-03-15T10:02:19Z] provisioning: PXE boot started for node-rtx-45
[2026-03-15T10:03:45Z] provisioning: PXE timeout waiting for image for node-rtx-45
[2026-03-15T10:03:46Z] autoscaler: mark node-rtx-45 FAILED, retry=1
[2026-03-15T10:04:00Z] autoscaler: desired=20 current=12 pending=8 rate_limit=1/s
[2026-03-15T10:04:12Z] kubelet: image pull backoff on node-rtx-32: registry-latency
```
evans: infra here — seeing the same. Our PXE servers (pxe01/pxe02) are saturated and the DHCP pool for that customer subnet is hitting lease exhaustion; many nodes keep retrying and timing out. Also the image registry for that onprem site has intermittent 503s, compounding boot retries.
evan: immediate options: increase DHCP lease pool & restart pxe services OR divert traffic to hosted fallback while we fix provisioning.
jamal: we should mitigate customer impact now. cust-support: what's the customer impact?
cust-support: medica reports ~18% request error rate and model latency jumped from 240ms to 9.8s. They say some inference jobs are queueing for minutes. SLA alert fired to them and to our SRE.
sara: ok, priority = high customer-impact. Steps: 1) route a fraction of traffic to hosted fallback; 2) attempt to increase provisioning concurrency; 3) keep autoscaler rate limit unchanged until infra confirms PXE/DHCP improvements.
carmen: will do step 1 routing. jamal, can you prepare the routing command?
jamal: running routing change to send up to 50% of medica traffic to hosted-dedicated-fallback (GPU-variants) with graceful fallback. command:```sh
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --customer medica --from cluster-17 --to hosted-dedicated-fallback --max-percent 50 --ttl 60s
```
ops-oncall: make sure we set a slow ramp to avoid sudden load on hosted. start at 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 5 minutes.
carmen: ops-oncall confirmed, I'll execute ramp. executing 10% now. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: routing change applied: medica 10% -> hosted-dedicated-fallback. monitoring latency & error rates.
jamal: infra, can you attempt to expand DHCP pool and restart pxe01? evan?
evan: on it. Command sequence (executed):```sh
# increase DHCP reservation on subnet 10.254.12.0/24 by +64
dhcpctl expand-range --subnet 10.254.12.0/24 --add 64
systemctl restart pxe-service pxe-sync
```
evan: DHCP range expanded, pxe services restarted. also triggered a cache refresh on local registry node: `curl -X POST http://registry-local/refresh` — registry 503s spiked down after cache warm.
jamal: autoscaler pending nodes are now moving from BOOTING -> READY for 3 nodes. still some failures but rate of success trending up.
incident-bot: metric update: gpu_queue_length -> 210 (down from 315), request errors -> 12% (down from 18%).
cust-support: customer seeing fewer errors, posted a message thanking for rapid response.
sara: continue reroute ramp: 25% now. carmen: confirm rollout.
carmen: 25% applied. monitoring shows latency improvement: p95 down to 3.1s for medica.
jamal: final infra step — we should temporarily increase autoscaler rate_limit to 2/s to let provisioning catch up while DHCP stabilizes. evan, are you comfortable with that?
evan: yes temporarily. command run:```yaml
# autoscaler config patch
autoscaler:
  rate_limit: 2
  retry_backoff: 30s
```
evan: changed. watch for any downstream impact to PXE. so far so good.
incident-bot: autoscaler desired->20 current->17 pending->3. queue continuing to shrink.
ops-oncall: looks stable for now. set a 30m watch and follow-up with customer success. assign to sara for postmortem.
sara: taking postmortem. action items: 1) increase warm pool for onprem nodepools for customers with burst SLAs, 2) add DHCP exhaustion alert to infra channel, 3) harden registry cache and add pre-warm on provisioning path.
jamal: handing off to sara for follow-up and timeline. I'm staying in channel for 15m.
sara: thanks jamal — I'll do the write-up and coordinate with infra. cust-support, please send medica a brief update and ETA for full resolution.
cust-support: emailing now with summary and that we're monitoring; provided temporary mitigation steps and ETA 2h for full provisioning normalization.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> under watch. Severity: Sev2 (customer impact, partial degradation).
sara: closing active pager; continuing monitoring. I'll open postmortem ticket and include logs + timeline. please add any extra notes here. :memo:
